subject: Request: short public-facing DPA & Hosted API privacy blurbs for AcmeAnalytics
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@acmeanalytics.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Short customer-facing DPA/Hosted API snippet (one-pager)

Hi Jonas,

We're finalizing our vendor security appendix and need a 1-paragraph and a 1-line summary we can paste into the procurement doc that explains how Redwood handles customer data for the Hosted API and what safeguards apply to cross-border transfers. The reviewers want plain-language examples (e.g., what qualifies as "input" vs "logs") and a short note about subprocessors and where they can see the current list.

Could you send two versions:
- A short paragraph (2-3 sentences) suitable for public docs or the security appendix
- A one-line dot point that sales can paste into an SOW

Also, please flag any dependencies (SCCs, KMS options, retention controls) we should call out. We have a legal reviewer on copy (legal@acmeanalytics.com).

Thanks,
Marta
Head of Data & Security
Acme Analytics

--
Attachment: procurement-template.xlsx (reference - not attached here)

Jonas Weber

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Short customer-facing DPA/Hosted API snippet (one-pager)

Thanks for the ping — sketched two short options below. I prioritized clarity over legal terms; we can add a parenthetical with DPA/SCC references if legal wants them.

Option A (paragraph, 2 sentences):
Redwood Inference processes your API inputs to generate responses and temporarily stores short-lived operational metadata (like request timestamps and anonymized metrics) to ensure service reliability. We do not use customer inputs to train models unless you opt in, and cross-border transfers are protected by standard contractual safeguards — see our DPA. A current list of our service partners (subprocessors) and their locations is published at: https://console.redwood.ai/settings/subprocessors

Option B (paragraph, 2 sentences — simpler):
When you use Redwood's Hosted API, we process the text and data you send to return model outputs; we only keep minimal operational logs for performance and debugging. We protect transfers across borders with contractual safeguards and publish an up-to-date list of our service partners (subprocessors) on our console.

One-line sales bullet (concise):
Redwood processes your API inputs to produce outputs, retains minimal operational logs, and protects international transfers with contractual safeguards — subprocessor list: https://console.redwood.ai/settings/subprocessors

Notes / suggestions: 
- Swap the word "subprocessors" with "service partners" in public-facing UX (less legalese).
- Add a short parenthetical pointing to SCCs or our DPA for procurement/legal teams.
- If we publish a short FAQ example ("what counts as input vs logs"), that will reduce follow-up questions from customers.

Laura Bennett
Product Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 16:24:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Short customer-facing DPA/Hosted API snippet (one-pager)

Agree with Laura; Option B is clean for sales. A couple of points to include before we send to Acme's legal: 

- Call out transfers: add a short clause like "We rely on EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) and other safeguards where applicable; customers can request a Data Processing Addendum (DPA) that references these safeguards."
- Add a short line confirming KMS/HSM options for enterprise customers (we should reference the console page where they can enable customer-managed keys).
- For the public page use "service partners"; in the DPA/contract we keep "subprocessors".

Proposed one-line bullet (final):
Redwood processes your API inputs to produce outputs, retains minimal operational logs for reliability, and protects international transfers with contractual safeguards (SCCs) — service partners: https://console.redwood.ai/settings/subprocessors; enterprise KMS available.

If that looks good I can send a short note to Marta + attach the redwood-dpa-summary-v2.pdf and the two snippet options as a one-pager.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Data & Privacy
Redwood Inference
